research journal / 016

Neuroarchitecture research

Studies on how the spaces we build relate to the brain, summarised for architecture.

  1. 001

    Can your neighborhood change your brain?

    A Berlin study links neighborhood characteristics to brain changes in older adults.

  2. 002

    Can a view from the window help us heal?

    A small hospital study connects a view of trees with postoperative recovery.

  3. 003

    Does city living relate to how the brain handles stress?

    Current residence and urban upbringing show different associations with social stress responses.

  4. 004

    Are curved interiors judged more beautiful?

    An imaging study separates aesthetic preference from the wish to enter a room.

  5. 005

    Is nearby forest associated with brain structure?

    A Berlin study examines forest cover and MRI measures of the amygdala.

  6. 006

    What does one hour in the forest do to the brain?

    A randomized Berlin experiment compares forest and busy-street walks.

  7. 007

    Can campus courtyard design influence stress recovery?

    A virtual-reality experiment finds differences in skin conductance and perceived restorativeness, but not all physiological measures.

  8. 008

    Is neighborhood nature associated with dementia risk?

    A large UK cohort reports different associations for green space, water and cognitive diagnoses.

  9. 009

    Can forest microbes enter our homes?

    A small Finnish experiment tracks soil-associated microbes after forest soil is added to entrance rugs.

  10. 010

    Can a living wall influence responses to a demanding task?

    A small experiment finds a cardiac difference during a task, without a significant cognitive benefit.

  11. 011

    Can nature-themed art influence short-term brain responses?

    A virtual-room study examines EEG, blood pressure and perceived restoration after brief exposure.

  12. 012

    Can biodiverse daycare yards influence immune markers?

    A Finnish intervention links changes in yard biodiversity with microbiota and immune-regulation measures.

  13. 013

    How do home microbes relate to land use and asthma?

    A study of 95 homes finds different patterns for bacterial and fungal diversity.

  14. 014

    How do urban scenes relate to brain signals?

    An EEG study distinguishes early visual processing from later appraisal of street images.

  15. 015

    Does everyday green exposure relate to working memory?

    GPS and repeated assessments connect green exposure with momentary memory performance in older adults.

  16. 016

    Do office plants improve thinking, or only stress recovery?

    Four randomized VR experiments found short-term physiological effects of greenery, but no significant cognitive improvement.
